## Features and Tools

- **Install apps:** `mobile_install_app` installs from a file, "Install an app from file (.apk, .ipa, .app, .zip)". Related tools launch, terminate, list, and uninstall apps.
- **Screen recording:** `mobile_start_screen_recording` and `mobile_stop_screen_recording` record the device screen to a video file.
- **Sensors:** The page doesn't list a dedicated sensors tool. The closest are `mobile_set_location`, which overrides the reported GPS location, and orientation and fold controls.
- **Multiple devices:** `mobile_list_available_devices` lists simulators, emulators, and real devices. The same tools work across iOS and Android. Cloud devices can be reserved and released with `mobile_allocate_remote_device` and `mobile_release_remote_device`.
- **Other tools:** Screen interaction (taps, swipes, long presses, screenshots, element lists), text input and hardware buttons, deep links via `mobile_open_url`, device logs, crash reports, and batch commands.

## License

Apache-2.0.

## Requirements

- Xcode command line tools (iOS)
- Android Platform Tools (`adb`)
- Node.js v20+
- An MCP-compatible client, such as Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor
- A running simulator or emulator, or a connected real device with USB debugging or trust enabled

## Installation

**Quick install** (detects installed MCP clients and lets you choose which to configure):

```
npx @mobilenext/mobile-mcp@latest install
```

Add `--yes` to configure every detected client without prompting.

**Standard config JSON** (works in most clients):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "mobile-mcp": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@mobilenext/mobile-mcp@latest"]
    }
  }
}
```

**Claude Code** (plugin, which adds the server and `/mobile-mirror`):

```
/plugin marketplace add mobile-next/mobile-mcp
/plugin install mobile-mcp@mobile-mcp
```

**Claude Code** (MCP server only):

```
claude mcp add mobile-mcp -- npx -y @mobilenext/mobile-mcp@latest
```

Other clients have their own steps, such as `codex mcp add` for Codex and `gemini mcp add` for Gemini CLI. The README covers each one.

**AndroidBuildMCP** (`dev-jackson/androidbuild-mcp`) is an MCP server that gives AI agents Android build, device, and UI tools.

**License:** MIT. The README links to the LICENSE file.

**Requirements:** Node 18+, the Android SDK (via `ANDROID_HOME` or a default install), and JDK 17+ for Gradle builds.

**Install**

Claude Code:
```
claude mcp add androidbuild -- npx -y @asjackson/androidbuild-mcp
```

Other MCP clients:
```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "androidbuild": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@asjackson/androidbuild-mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

Run from source:
```
git clone https://github.com/dev-jackson/androidbuild-mcp.git
cd androidbuild-mcp
npm install && npm run build
claude mcp add androidbuild -- node /absolute/path/to/androidbuild-mcp/dist/index.js
```

After installing, ask the agent to run `doctor` to check your setup.

**Tools (53 over stdio)**

- **Environment and project (6):** doctor, discover_projects, list_modules, list_variants, get_app_id, show_gradle_config
- **Session defaults (3):** session_set_defaults, session_show_defaults, session_clear_defaults
- **Build, test, quality (10):** build_app, build_run, test_app, test_instrumented, lint, clean, get_apk_path, stop_gradle, get_coverage_report, get_file_coverage
- **Devices and emulators (9):** list_devices, list_avds, boot_emulator, kill_emulator, create_avd, delete_avd, set_emulator_location, set_appearance, statusbar_demo_mode
- **App lifecycle (6):** install_app, launch_app, stop_app, uninstall_app, clear_app_data, get_app_info
- **UI automation (12):** snapshot_ui, screenshot, tap_element, tap, scroll, swipe, drag, long_press, type_text, key_press, key_sequence, wait_for_ui
- **Logs and recording (6):** get_logs, get_crash_logs, start_log_capture, stop_log_capture, record_video_start, record_video_stop
- **Scaffolding (1):** scaffold_android_project

**Not covered in the page:** The content does not mention sensor or emulator console tools, rotation controls, or parallel multi-device operation. It only notes that the right device is auto-selected when one is connected.

**Maturity and activity**

- The README says every tool was tested against real emulators and projects, with evidence in `qa-results.md`.
- The repo has 0 stars, 0 watchers, and 2 forks, and 8 commits on `main`.
- The page does not show a release date or the date of the last update, and it lists no published releases.

**License:** MIT. The repo's About section links to the MIT license file.

**Tools:** The page lists 73 tools in one place and 80 in another. Relevant areas include:
- **Gradle build and test:** `assembleDebug`, unit tests, instrumented tests, JaCoCo coverage reports, and a one-shot `build_and_run`. Builds can run in the background.
- **Screen recording:** Included under Logs & capture.
- **Sensors:** `set_sensor` for accelerometer, light, and similar sensors (emulator).
- **Rotation:** `rotate_screen` (emulator).
- **Device locks:** Set or clear a secure lock screen and check lock state. Biometric tools can satisfy a BiometricPrompt on the emulator.
- **Multiple devices:** Tools take an optional `serial`, and `list_devices` shows attached devices. The page doesn't explicitly say that operations run in parallel across devices.
- **Also:** Install and uninstall apps, screenshots, UI hierarchy, tap/swipe/type, logcat, and Wi-Fi connection.

**Install commands:**
- macOS/Linux installer: `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/iksnerd/adb-mcp/main/install.sh | sh`
- Update: `adb-mcp update`
- Claude Code: `claude mcp add adb -- adb-mcp`
- Claude plugin: `claude plugin marketplace add iksnerd/adb-mcp`, then `claude plugin install adb-mcp@adb-mcp`
- Codex plugin: `codex plugin marketplace add iksnerd/adb-mcp`, then `codex plugin add adb-mcp@adb-mcp-plugins`
- From source: `go install github.com/iksnerd/adb-mcp/cmd/adb-mcp@latest`

**MCP config JSON:**
```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "adb": { "command": "adb-mcp" }
  }
}
```

**Requirements:**
- Android SDK with `platform-tools` (adb) and `emulator`. The server finds it through `$ANDROID_HOME`/`$ANDROID_SDK_ROOT` or the platform default. Otherwise pass `--sdk`.
- At least one AVD.
- `adb-mcp` on your PATH (or an absolute path to the binary).
- Go 1.26+ only for building from source. Prebuilt binaries don't need it.
- Node on your PATH for the Claude plugin. The Codex plugin still needs `adb-mcp` on your PATH.

**Maturity:** The page doesn't state a stability level. It shows versioned releases (the install example pins v0.24.3), CI badges, a security policy, and a contributing guide. It has 115 commits, 15 stars, and 4 forks. The project is public and actively developed, but the page doesn't call it production-ready.

content.text:
I recommend **adb-mcp** ([iksnerd/adb-mcp](https://github.com/iksnerd/adb-mcp)). It's MIT-licensed, free, and a standard stdio MCP server written in Go. One caveat applies to every option: no MCP server finds bugs or judges quality on its own. The server gives the LLM tools to build, install, tap, type, take screenshots, record the screen, read logcat and run tests. Your MCP client's LLM (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, etc.) does the exploring and decides what counts as a bug. That's enough to automate your loop.

## Why adb-mcp fits best

From its README, which I read but haven't tested:

- **Build and test:** Gradle `assembleDebug`, a one-step `build_and_run`, unit tests, instrumented tests, JaCoCo coverage reports, and builds that run in the background.
- **Install and run:** install and uninstall apps, launch them, read logcat.
- **Test like a person:** screenshots, the UI element tree, tap/swipe/type, and **screen recording**.
- **Sensors:** `set_sensor` (accelerometer, light, etc.) and `rotate_screen`, plus lock-screen and biometric helpers. **These only work on emulators.** On a physical phone, adb can't fake sensor readings, so tilting still has to be done by hand or with a test-only hook in your app.
- **Devices:** works with real phones over USB or Wi-Fi and with emulators. Every tool accepts an optional device `serial`. **It doesn't promise true parallel runs.** To get them, I'm assuming you'd start one agent or session per device, each tied to its own serial, or ask one agent to switch between serials.
- **Maturity:** about 115 commits, versioned releases (v0.24.x), CI. It's young but actively maintained.

## Install and first run (macOS)

1. Prerequisites: install the Android SDK with `platform-tools` (adb) and `emulator`, set `ANDROID_HOME`, and create at least one AVD. Building your app also needs a JDK, usually 17 or later.
2. Install the server. Pick one:
   - From source (needs Go 1.26+): `go install github.com/iksnerd/adb-mcp/cmd/adb-mcp@latest`
   - The installer: `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/iksnerd/adb-mcp/main/install.sh | sh`. Read the script before piping it to `sh`.
3. Register it with your client:
   - Claude Code: `claude mcp add adb -- adb-mcp`
   - Other clients: `{"mcpServers": {"adb": {"command": "adb-mcp"}}}`
4. Plug in your phone with USB debugging on, run `adb devices`, and accept the authorization prompt on the phone.
5. First prompt, from your project folder:
   > "List devices. Build the debug APK and install/launch it on device `<serial>`. Start a screen recording, then explore the new <feature>: tap every control, enter valid/invalid/empty text, rotate, background and resume the app. Check logcat for crashes/ANRs after each step. Stop the recording, then write a bug list with steps to reproduce, and fix each bug, rebuild and re-verify."
6. For parallel testing, open a second session, assign it another serial (for example an emulator for the sensor tests), and give it a different area of the app to test.

## Alternatives

- **[AndroidBuildMCP](https://github.com/dev-jackson/androidbuild-mcp)** (MIT): build_app/build_run with compiler errors as file:line, tests, coverage, recording (3-minute cap), and AVD management. It has no sensor tools, and it's very new (8 commits, 0 stars). Install with `claude mcp add androidbuild -- npx -y @asjackson/androidbuild-mcp`, then ask it to run `doctor`.
- **[mobile-mcp](https://github.com/mobile-next/mobile-mcp)** (Apache-2.0): the most widely used device-control server. It supports Android and iOS, real devices and emulators, screen recording and crash logs. It **doesn't build**, so you'd pair it with Gradle in your client's shell. Install with `claude mcp add mobile-mcp -- npx -y @mobilenext/mobile-mcp@latest`.
- I also found [mcp-android-emulator](https://github.com/Anjos2/mcp-android-emulator) and [android-mcp-server](https://github.com/jaye773/android-mcp-server), which both have recording but no builds. I didn't check them in detail.

## Tips

- Have the agent save each bug it finds as a repeatable test (an Espresso test or a scripted flow). Then every later round re-checks the earlier fixes, and the coverage reports give you a real "how well is it going" number.
- On a real phone, Android's built-in recorder (`adb screenrecord`) stops after about 3 minutes. Ask the agent to record in short pieces.
- You still need your manual code review at the end. These tools can confirm the app behaves correctly, not that the code is good.

Sources: [adb-mcp](https://github.com/iksnerd/adb-mcp), [androidbuild-mcp](https://github.com/dev-jackson/androidbuild-mcp), [mobile-mcp](https://github.com/mobile-next/mobile-mcp), [mcp-android-emulator](https://github.com/Anjos2/mcp-android-emulator), [android-mcp-server](https://github.com/jaye773/android-mcp-server), [android-phone-mcp](https://github.com/liush2yuxjtu/android-phone-mcp)

## Why adb-mcp fits best

From its README, which I read but haven't tested:

- **Build and test:** Gradle `assembleDebug`, a one-step `build_and_run`, unit tests, instrumented tests, JaCoCo coverage reports, and builds that run in the background.
- **Install and run:** install and uninstall apps, launch them, read logcat.
- **Test like a person:** screenshots, the UI element tree, tap/swipe/type, and **screen recording**.
- **Sensors:** `set_sensor` (accelerometer, light, etc.) and `rotate_screen`, plus lock-screen and biometric helpers. **These only work on emulators.** On a physical phone, adb can't fake sensor readings, so tilting still has to be done by hand or with a test-only hook in your app.
- **Devices:** works with real phones over USB or Wi-Fi and with emulators. Every tool accepts an optional device `serial`. **It doesn't promise true parallel runs.** To get them, I'm assuming you'd start one agent or session per device, each tied to its own serial, or ask one agent to switch between serials.
- **Maturity:** about 115 commits, versioned releases (v0.24.x), CI. It's young but actively maintained.

## Install and first run (macOS)

1. Prerequisites: install the Android SDK with `platform-tools` (adb) and `emulator`, set `ANDROID_HOME`, and create at least one AVD. Building your app also needs a JDK, usually 17 or later.
2. Install the server. Pick one:
   - From source (needs Go 1.26+): `go install github.com/iksnerd/adb-mcp/cmd/adb-mcp@latest`
   - The installer: `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/iksnerd/adb-mcp/main/install.sh | sh`. Read the script before piping it to `sh`.
3. Register it with your client:
   - Claude Code: `claude mcp add adb -- adb-mcp`
   - Other clients: `{"mcpServers": {"adb": {"command": "adb-mcp"}}}`
4. Plug in your phone with USB debugging on, run `adb devices`, and accept the authorization prompt on the phone.
5. First prompt, from your project folder:
   > "List devices. Build the debug APK and install/launch it on device `<serial>`. Start a screen recording, then explore the new <feature>: tap every control, enter valid/invalid/empty text, rotate, background and resume the app. Check logcat for crashes/ANRs after each step. Stop the recording, then write a bug list with steps to reproduce, and fix each bug, rebuild and re-verify."
6. For parallel testing, open a second session, assign it another serial (for example an emulator for the sensor tests), and give it a different area of the app to test.

## Alternatives

- **[AndroidBuildMCP](https://github.com/dev-jackson/androidbuild-mcp)** (MIT): build_app/build_run with compiler errors as file:line, tests, coverage, recording (3-minute cap), and AVD management. It has no sensor tools, and it's very new (8 commits, 0 stars). Install with `claude mcp add androidbuild -- npx -y @asjackson/androidbuild-mcp`, then ask it to run `doctor`.
- **[mobile-mcp](https://github.com/mobile-next/mobile-mcp)** (Apache-2.0): the most widely used device-control server. It supports Android and iOS, real devices and emulators, screen recording and crash logs. It **doesn't build**, so you'd pair it with Gradle in your client's shell. Install with `claude mcp add mobile-mcp -- npx -y @mobilenext/mobile-mcp@latest`.
- I also found [mcp-android-emulator](https://github.com/Anjos2/mcp-android-emulator) and [android-mcp-server](https://github.com/jaye773/android-mcp-server), which both have recording but no builds. I didn't check them in detail.

## Tips

- Have the agent save each bug it finds as a repeatable test (an Espresso test or a scripted flow). Then every later round re-checks the earlier fixes, and the coverage reports give you a real "how well is it going" number.
- On a real phone, Android's built-in recorder (`adb screenrecord`) stops after about 3 minutes. Ask the agent to record in short pieces.
- You still need your manual code review at the end. These tools can confirm the app behaves correctly, not that the code is good.

Sources: [adb-mcp](https://github.com/iksnerd/adb-mcp), [androidbuild-mcp](https://github.com/dev-jackson/androidbuild-mcp), [mobile-mcp](https://github.com/mobile-next/mobile-mcp), [mcp-android-emulator](https://github.com/Anjos2/mcp-android-emulator), [android-mcp-server](https://github.com/jaye773/android-mcp-server), [android-phone-mcp](https://github.com/liush2yuxjtu/android-phone-mcp)
